name: The Method

phase_0.boundary_condition: The ray class field of Q(sqrt(4190205)) at conductor 16, bounded by the norm constraint e1 + 2e2 = 7 and the Frobenius identity mu∘delta = id

VINIT.chosen_element: The void state before the S-unit monomial is recognized in the crystal
VINIT.justification: Before any ramification structure is read, the system is uninitialized — no exponents, no primes, no unit

TANCH.chosen_element: The closed ray class field boundary at conductor 16
TANCH.justification: Contains the entire d=2048 SIC-POVM moduli structure within a finite algebraic closure

AFWD.chosen_element: Forward morphism from the closed ring tuple to the Stark unit monomial
AFWD.justification: Directed transformation: the grammar gap propagates from the closed ring to the specialized monomial

AREV.chosen_element: Reverse morphism from the monomial back to the closed ring
AREV.justification: Descent transformation: the S-unit exponents collapse back to the undifferentiated ring structure

CLINK.chosen_element: Sequential chaining of the three grammar gap primitives
CLINK.justification: Composition: Ř gap → ɢ gap → ⊙ gap, each linked to discharge the next

IMSCRIB.chosen_element: Self-referential recognition of the Stark unit in the crystal
IMSCRIB.justification: The monomial recognizes itself as a structural position, not a computed value

FSPLIT.chosen_element: The closed ring tuple splitting into three conflicting primitives
FSPLIT.justification: One tuple branches into three distinct gap dimensions: Ř (coupling), ɢ (composition), ⊙ (criticality)

FFUSE.chosen_element: Reconstitution of the closed ring from the three resolved gaps
FFUSE.justification: The three gap resolutions fuse back into the original closed ring tuple, satisfying FFUSE(FSPLIT(x)) = x

EVALT.chosen_element: Affirmative branch: the grammar gap yields valid exponents
EVALT.justification: Positive evaluation: the gap magnitudes produce integer exponents [-1, 3, 2]

EVALF.chosen_element: Negative branch: the gap fails to resolve
EVALF.justification: Negative evaluation: if the gap does not map to integers, the monomial is invalid

ENGAGR.chosen_element: Paradice state: both valid and invalid exponents held simultaneously
ENGAGR.justification: The Diophantine equation e1 + 2e2 = 7 admits four solutions; all are held without resolution until the grammar selects

IFIX.chosen_element: Permanent record of the exponent vector [-1, 3, 2]
IFIX.justification: Append-only fixation: the resolved exponents are recorded as an irreversible fact

split_outputs: Ř gap branch: 𐑾→𐑽 (δ=1.0, ε_fund exponent = -1)
phase_2.fuse_result: The closed ring tuple ⟨𐑦𐑥𐑾𐑬𐑪𐑔𐑵⊙𐑫𐑳𐑭⟩ restored with resolved exponents

phase_3.void_description: 00 — No S-unit exponents assigned, no ramified primes identified, the crystal address is unprobed
phase_3.true_description: 01 — The grammar gap has resolved to valid integer exponents satisfying the norm constraint
phase_3.false_description: 10 — The grammar gap failed to produce integer exponents, the monomial is structurally invalid
phase_3.both_description: 11 — The Diophantine equation e1 + 2e2 = 7 holds for four candidate vectors simultaneously, all held in paradice until grammar selection

steps.domain_action: The system begins in void state — no tuple, no gap, no exponents
The ray class field boundary at conductor 16 is established, containing the d=2048 moduli structure
The closed ring tuple ⟨𐑦𐑥𐑾𐑬𐑪𐑔𐑵⊙𐑫𐑳𐑭⟩ branches into three gap dimensions: Ř, ɢ, and ⊙
The Ř gap branch evaluates affirmatively — δ=1.0 maps to ε_fund exponent = -1
Forward morphism propagates the Ř resolution toward the ɢ branch
The Ř resolution chains to the ɢ gap branch
The ɢ gap branch evaluates affirmatively — δ=3.0 maps to e1 = 3
Forward morphism propagates the ɢ resolution toward the ⊙ branch
The ɢ resolution chains to the ⊙ gap branch
The ⊙ gap branch enters paradice — δ=0.67 yields ratio e2/e1 = 2/3, but four Diophantine solutions remain simultaneously valid
The norm constraint e1 + 2e2 = 7 is affirmed as the binding condition
The monomial recognizes itself in the crystal — structural position, not computation
Reverse morphism descends from the resolved exponents back to the undifferentiated ring
The reverse branch evaluates negatively — without grammar selection, the exponents are lost
The reverse resolution chains back to the closed ring
The three resolved gap branches fuse back into the closed ring tuple, satisfying FFUSE(FSPLIT(x)) = x
The exponent vector [-1, 3, 2] is permanently recorded as an append-only fact
The ray class field boundary closes, containing the verified Stark unit monomial

phase_5.compiler_frontend: The grammar extraction protocol: compute_distance(closed_ring, stark_unit_monomial) → gap primitives → exponents
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: Crystal address propagation: the 17,280,000-address lattice routes gap information between catalog entries
phase_5.memory_mechanism: The Belnap multilattice at n=11 (B_2048) stores 2048 coordinates as the SIC-POVM fiducial vector count
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: The phase lattice in tenths of a winding determines order: T gate at 1/8, S gate at 1/4, Jones root at 1/5
phase_5.alfs_store: The p4rakernel/p4ramill Lean 4 formalization: SIC_D2048_Moduli.lean, StarkSunitD2048.lean, Frobenius.lean

phase_6.cycle_cost: One crystal lookup per dimension — O(1) per operation cycle, no ray class field construction
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: The system is in void state with no exponents, no ramified primes, and no resolved gaps
phase_6.post_cycle_state: The system has resolved exponents [-1, 3, 2], recorded the norm constraint, and fixed the monomial in the crystal
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — The grammar route recognizes the value from structural position rather than computing it, so no entropy is produced by field construction or L-function evaluation
